processSection.title: How the engagement is structured
processSection.sidebarTitle: Each matter moves through diagnosis, an initial route, and verifiable follow-through.

processCards.title: 1. Context intake
processCards.description: Facts, urgency, parties involved, and the client's practical objective are identified before any course of action is suggested.

processCards.title: 2. Initial document review
processCards.description: Documents are organized, missing information is detected, and points with possible legal or operational impact are flagged.

processCards.title: 3. Suggested route
processCards.description: An initial action scheme is proposed with priorities, dependencies, and scenarios to support informed decisions.

processCards.title: 4. Follow-through and adjustments
processCards.description: Support continues through useful communication, ongoing review, and adjustments when the matter changes direction.

faqSection.title: Frequently asked questions
faqSection.subtitle: General answers to orient the visitor before requesting an initial assessment.

faq.title: Does the first conversation replace full legal advice?
faq.content: No. The first assessment is meant to understand the context, identify urgency, and define whether document review, preventive advisory, or a broader strategy is appropriate.

faq.title: What should be prepared before reaching out?
faq.content: It is best to gather agreements, communications, IDs, corporate records, and any documents that help explain the issue accurately.

faq.title: Can the practice assist both companies and individuals?
faq.content: Yes. The draft is framed for corporate advisory and related civil matters, always subject to the actual scope of the case.

faq.title: What happens after the first contact?
faq.content: An initial route is suggested with priorities, required documents, and possible next steps so the client can make better-informed decisions.
